hook.text: The internet was supposed to be global. Instead, it's splitting into Chinese, Russian, European, and American zones.

buildup.text: Each zone has different rules. China blocks Western apps. Russia demands local data storage. The EU mandates privacy.

discovery.text: The 'splinternet' means people in different countries experience fundamentally different versions of the online world.

twist.text: Tech firms adapt by building separate products for each zone. TikTok runs a different algorithm in China than abroad.

climax.text: If the internet fractures completely, the idea of a global public square dies. Each zone becomes its own reality.

punchline.text: One internet was a dream. Many internets is the reality.

quiz.question: What does the 'splinternet' refer to?
options: The internet fragmenting into regional zones
